about: The creative director's TASTE RULES: lessons that a number can check, run on every preset by `kit vfx director lint <name>` (and inside review). A rule is born from a recording or a verdict that went wrong; add one whenever a lesson is measurable (type = one of the checks in kit/vfx/director.py LINTS). The point: a mistake caught once is caught forever, on every future effect. Every rule is CALIBRATED: `kit vfx director calibrate` runs it on the loved set (it must never fire there) and the rejected set (it should) - a rule that condemns a loved piece is narrowed until it holds.

rules.lesson: trails on a flock of hundreds draw HAIR, not birds: a murmuration is dots; keep trails for sparks and scatter (a few hundred at most)
a swarm dot under ~0.55% of the camera distance (0.15 studs at 30) vanishes: the mass is there but does not read (trailed swarms read as streaks and are exempt: nuke_v4)

a WIDE-band ground ring (band >= 0.2 of its radius, or strands) wider than ~0.6 of the hero camera's distance fills the floor as a flat plate; size it to the effect (thin travelling rings are fine - until they reach ~0.9 of the camera distance and sweep past it as fat bands: resonance round 3)

grey or pale unlit cel smoke under a warm / day sky reads as a stack of grey ROCKS - even tinted rosy [236, 214, 206] (round 3): the cel shadow bands go grey under that light; drop it, light it (lightEmission) or use a dust that belongs to the scene

untextured Neon reads as plastic when it is a SHARE of the effect (>= 20 % of the meshes) or a VOLUME (sphere / spikes / cone / spiral ...); air / energy is never a solid surface (rasengan 'looks horrible', the all-mesh saiyans 'so bad'). Calibrated: a few accent rings are fine (starblade 9.5, saiyan_ssj_3d 9.0)

a big glowing ground decal in a saturated colour on a LIGHT ground (sand) reads as a flat coloured plate (vermilion cracks became a pink disc) - mute it or keep the ground answer to crest / rocks / dust

a handful of giant CEL smoke puffs (<= 5 particles, >= 10 studs) reads as a stack of ROCKS / a tower, not a bloom: more, smaller, faster puffs with a wider spread. (Lit simulated smoke is exempt: one sim sprite is a whole volume - nuke_v4, loved at 8.7, is a single 140-stud sprite; the rule once flagged lit steam, 2026-10-24)
a bright saturated point light near a LIGHT ground paints a coloured disc on it that reads as a flat plate (vermilion -> pink, violet -> lilac); keep hit lights white-ish, high, or off a light floor
echoes of a translucent Neon RING stack into one solid dish (4 notes x 4 copies of a 0.12 band = a teal bowl): one echo at most, hairline width

a wide-band (>= 0.2 of its radius) saturated Neon ground ring is translucent: on a LIGHT ground it reads as a coloured plate at ANY size (vermilion -> pink, violet -> lilac) - a dark ground, an ink / opaque ring, or no crest
a strong rim (transparency < 0.6) on a SMALL mesh (< 1 stud) makes it a glowing pearl - energy, not matter; for a material's sheen keep the rim faint (>= 0.75) and in the object's own colour

impact frames draw only lit Lambert shapes (actor, debris, Lambert swarms -> ink) and bright saturated layers (-> energy); at a framed hit something drawable must be alive AND grown - hoarfrost's frames at a Glass, still-flat eruption were empty for 4 rounds. Move the frames to the beat whose shapes are drawable at their peak

slash frames (draw.slash / split, lines 'cut') read the cut line from an ARC alive at the hit; a sweep starting at zero length has no centreline there and the frames draw nothing - enter the cut partly drawn or keep a guide arc alive across the hit

smoke / steam / dust is ONE simulated event card, never a swarm of LIT puff cards: each lit card is lit on its own and reads as a lump (cotton balls, rocks) - quenchstrike 'The Effects like Smoke looks horrible' (27 lit gpu_smoke puffs), nuke_v3 'the smoke looks bad around' and nuke_v2 'the smoke around it' (4-6 lit puff emitters round the mushroom) vs nuke_v4 8.7 (the same mushroom + ONE simulated surge card). Simulate the event (kit/vfx/gpusim.py surge / stem / swirl) as one lit card; unlit sim puffs blending into one wall are fine (starblade 9.5)

evidence.words: The Effects like Smoke looks horrible
the smoke looks bad around and the explosion cutzx off at the top
could be improved in ways like the smoke around it and how it fades

rules.lesson: an untextured SOLID mesh (SmoothPlastic / Plastic / Metal ..., no texture, no surface) reads as low-quality plastic when it is a share of the effect (>= 20 % of the meshes) or a VOLUME (sphere, tube, spikes ...): quicksilver's 8 untextured SmoothPlastic meshes - 'Meshs ... very low quality'. Skin it (a texture made for its UV axis, or a surface); not asked: Glass, ForceField, a mirror (reflectance >= 0.3), a near-black void. untextured-neon-mesh asks Neon

evidence.words: Meshs and Impact frames very low quality

rules.lesson: a whole technique built as a THIN stack - few kinds of layer, mostly flat sprites - reads cheap beside his loved pieces: flame_arc (REDO 2026-11-11: 'Does not look high quality ... genuine dookie') was 61 layers of 5 kinds, 85 % sprites; flame_arc_keybeat (REDO 2026-11-10) 10 layers of 3 kinds, 80 % sprites. His loved pieces use 7-13 kinds and at most 67 % sprites; starblade r6 (9.5) is 148 layers of 13 kinds - mesh shells, beams, lights, screen + fov + shake, decals, debris, a trail, a glow, sound. Build the key beat's look from meshes + rendered textures + light + camera + ground, not from more sprites

evidence.words: it's generally so bad. Does not look high quality. Does not look like the thing you want ... This looks like genuine dookie
even if it's just a slash, it just doesn't look good. It doesn't look high quality
